Course_Brief.learner_context: Mixed-readiness secondary learners developing evidence-based reading, interaction and process writing.
Course_Brief.required_content: Reading, writing, speaking, listening, language in context and multimodal literacy.
Course_Brief.assessment_pattern: Reading/writing/oral evidence; semester assessments; feedback and revision after each major task.
Course_Brief.resource_constraints: School-developed materials, library texts and accessible digital publishing tools.
Course_Brief.mc_focus: MC2;MC3, with MC1 where a real intercultural audience strengthens language learning.
Course_Brief.authority_title: English Language Education Key Learning Area Curriculum Guide (Primary 1–Secondary 6)
Course_Brief.authority_section: Secondary framework — exact chapter requires teacher confirmation
Course_Brief.notes: Forward-test sample only; not an approved MINXIN course.

Course_Brief.learner_context: Mixed-readiness learners who benefit from explicit representation, variation, retrieval and diagnostic feedback.
Course_Brief.required_content: Number and algebra, linear relationships, geometry, probability/statistics, reasoning and problem solving.
Course_Brief.assessment_pattern: Short diagnostic checks, worked reasoning, cumulative problem sets and semester assessments.
Course_Brief.resource_constraints: School-developed examples, graph paper, manipulatives, dynamic geometry and calculators where justified.
Course_Brief.mc_focus: MC2 through rigorous research-informed mathematics teaching; MC3 through perseverance and self-regulation.
Course_Brief.authority_title: Mathematics Education Key Learning Area Curriculum Guide (Primary 1–Secondary 6)
Course_Brief.authority_section: Key Stage 3 — exact chapter requires teacher confirmation
Course_Brief.notes: No forced AI, project, group presentation or business-analysis component.

Course_Brief.learner_context: Learners developing visual inquiry, technique, critique vocabulary, authorship and independent portfolio habits.
Course_Brief.required_content: Appreciation, contextual research, media experimentation, making, critique, portfolio documentation and revision.
Course_Brief.assessment_pattern: Process portfolio, technical studies, critique response, resolved work and individual artist statement.
Course_Brief.resource_constraints: Drawing/painting media, recycled materials, cameras/tablets, safe cutting tools and display space.
Course_Brief.mc_focus: MC2 through iterative studio practice; MC3 through identity, critique and leadership; selective MC1 global comparison.
Course_Brief.authority_title: Arts Education Key Learning Area Curriculum Guide (Primary 1–Secondary 6)
Course_Brief.authority_section: Visual Arts at Key Stage 3 — exact chapter requires teacher confirmation
Course_Brief.notes: Digital/AI media are considered only where authorship, rights and verification are teachable visual-arts concerns.

Units.title: Reading Evidence and Voice
Units.essential_question: How does a writer position a reader?
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students revise an interpretation after comparing cited evidence.

Units.title: Writing for Real Readers
Units.essential_question: How do purpose and audience shape language choices?
Units.disciplinary_practice: process writing and language choices in context
Units.expected_evidence: revised feature article and writer's note
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students publish for a school audience and explain an intercultural language choice.

Units.title: Speaking, Listening and Viewpoints
Units.essential_question: How can dialogue deepen rather than flatten disagreement?
Units.disciplinary_practice: oral interaction, listening and source-informed response
Units.expected_evidence: individual speaking record and listening reflection
Units.major_concern_evidence: Rotating facilitators support dialogue; each student submits individual evidence.

Units.title: Comparative and Multimodal Texts
Units.essential_question: How do medium and culture change meaning?
Units.expected_evidence: comparative response and revised multimodal text
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students compare perspectives from more than one context and justify source use.

Units.title: Assessment Response and Independent Transfer
Units.essential_question: How does feedback become a stronger independent performance?
Units.expected_evidence: correction log, transfer task and learning reflection
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students use evidence from errors and feedback to set and test a personal target.

Units.title: Number Structure and Algebraic Generalisation
Units.essential_question: What structure stays invariant when representations change?
Units.expected_evidence: worked reasoning and cumulative problem set
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students compare solution evidence and revise an invalid generalisation.

Units.title: Linear Relationships
Units.essential_question: How do representations reveal rate and initial value?
Units.disciplinary_practice: connecting tables, graphs, equations and contexts
Units.expected_evidence: representation map and unfamiliar modelling problem
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students justify which representation exposes a relationship most clearly.

Units.title: Geometry and Deductive Reasoning
Units.essential_question: When is a geometric claim necessarily true?
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students persevere through counterexamples and improve a proof using feedback.

Units.title: Probability and Data Reasoning
Units.essential_question: How strong is the evidence for a claim about chance or data?
Units.expected_evidence: data critique and probability reasoning task
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students compare contextual data responsibly and state limits of inference.

Units.title: Assessment Diagnosis and Transfer
Units.essential_question: Which error pattern matters, and how can it be repaired?
Units.disciplinary_practice: error analysis, deliberate re-practice and transfer
Units.expected_evidence: error taxonomy, corrected solution and transfer check
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students select an error pattern, plan re-practice and verify improvement.

Units.title: Observation, Material and Visual Language
Units.essential_question: How do material choices direct attention?
Units.disciplinary_practice: observational inquiry, media control and visual analysis
Units.expected_evidence: technical studies and annotated process pages
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students compare trials and revise a material decision using visual evidence.

Units.title: Place, Identity and Visual Narrative
Units.essential_question: How can a visual narrative hold more than one perspective on place?
Units.disciplinary_practice: contextual research, composition and visual storytelling
Units.expected_evidence: resolved place narrative and artist note
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students represent local/global viewpoints responsibly and explain an individual choice.

Units.title: Critique, Authorship and Digital Collage
Units.essential_question: How do selection, transformation and attribution shape authorship?
Units.disciplinary_practice: source evaluation, digital composition, critique and revision
Units.expected_evidence: source log, collage iterations and critique response
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students document rights/source decisions and revise after evidence-based critique.

Units.title: Independent Body of Work
Units.essential_question: How does sustained inquiry become a coherent body of work?
Units.disciplinary_practice: independent inquiry, technique, curation and reflection
Units.expected_evidence: resolved work, process portfolio and artist statement
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students manage milestones, lead one studio handover and defend curatorial choices.

Units.title: Portfolio Review and Transfer
Units.essential_question: What does the portfolio reveal about artistic growth?
Units.expected_evidence: revised portfolio sequence and next-step study
Units.major_concern_evidence: Students cite portfolio evidence to evaluate progress and plan a new direction.
